description: Horizontal cross-section through the bottom fixed light (item '2' in the elevation drawing), cut through the post (mullion), sash, glazing bead, and glass of a fixed (non-opening) light.
extrusionAxis: Y (this cross section is extruded along the window WIDTH for a horizontal member; do not confuse with the vertical profile's Z/height extrusion)

verticalToHorizontalTransform.confirmedVia: GSK_SSH_EXT_HORIZONTAL gasket bbox vs vertical GSK_SSH_EXT bbox, residual < 0.02mm
verticalToHorizontalTransform.note: This transform is specific to this profile instance (F1XXX bottom fix). Re-derive per-profile using the dualColorSeamTransfer method in assemblyRules.json -- do not assume this same (0, 41.0) offset applies to other window sizes or other members.

assemblyOrigin.description: Reference point used to position this cross-section slice along the extrusion path in the full 3D assembly. Matches the assemblyOrigin/anchorPoints convention used in the vertical FRM/SSH pipeline.
assemblyOrigin.definedAs: Exterior-facing corner of the post profile at its lowest x, lowest y vertex in local section coordinates

sashSeamPoints.description: The two points where SSH_EXT_HORIZONTAL and SSH_INT_HORIZONTAL meet (dual-color cap seam). Useful as a stable registration feature if this profile needs to be re-aligned against future DXF revisions.

postSeamPoints.description: The two points where POST_EXT_HORIZONTAL and POST_INT_HORIZONTAL meet. Derived from the vertical FRM_EXT/FRM_INT seam (the post is the same extrusion as the frame), residual 0.38mm -- looser than the sash match because the source seam coordinate was only known to ~1mm precision, not because the transform is wrong.

knownIssuesFixed: POLYLINE closed-flag implicit closing segment was not being added, causing the post's interior-facing wall to appear missing. Fixed in flatten_horizontal.py -- now appends first vertex when closed=True and not already coincident.
FRM_HORIZONTAL source layer name renamed to POST_HORIZONTAL, then split -- it is physically the mullion/post (nested inside block 'słupek 01'), not the window frame.
SSH_HORIZONTAL (single merged sash outline) split into SSH_EXT_HORIZONTAL / SSH_INT_HORIZONTAL via seam transfer from the vertical reference file.

POST_HORIZONTAL (single merged post outline) split into POST_EXT_HORIZONTAL / POST_INT_HORIZONTAL via seam transfer from the vertical FRM_EXT/FRM_INT reference (the post is the same extrusion as the frame).
openQuestions: SPACER_SSH_HORIZONAL renders as a small isolated rectangle disconnected from the glass pane outlines -- geometrically plausible (spacer drawn separately from glass edges in source DXF) but not yet visually verified against the original AutoCAD file. Confirm before treating its position as a reliable anchor.
